album.title: Album
books.locked: The books are in order now. Best to leave them.
books5.readonly: The books stand as the reflection arranged them. You can't change them from here.
c1.ash: Ash. Cold, and very fine, like something that was a long time ago.
c1.books_look: Four books stand out from the others, each with its own colour and pattern. Their order feels wrong.
c1.books_solved: The last book slides into place. Somewhere below, a catch lets go: the cabinet door swings open.
c1.books_sorted: Red stripes, green dots, pale chevrons, plain yellow: just as in the painting.
c1.cabinet_shut: The cabinet door is shut fast. There is no keyhole. Something else holds it.
c1.candle_already: The candle is already burning. The match would only be wasted.
c1.candle_lit: The match flares. The candle takes it, grudgingly.
c1.candle_take: You lift the burning candle from its saucer, shielding the flame with your hand.
c1.candle_unlit: A candle stub on the mantel. It has never been lit, or has been lit too often.
c1.chart_take: A chart of the lake, pinned beside the window. You take it. Something in the margin makes you uneasy.
c1.clock_set: The hands stop. Something inside the case clicks, and a little hatch swings open.
c1.door_unlocked: Something clunks deep in the door. It swings open onto the jetty and the fog beyond.
c1.drawer_locked: The drawer has a brass-rimmed keyhole. Locked.
c1.drawer_open: The key turns. The drawer slides open.
c1.fish_engraving: A tiny fish is engraved on the clock face, right beside the four.
c1.food_take: A tin of fish food, labelled with a drawing of a fish. Whoever wrote the label had a sense of humour.
c1.hatch_open: The hatch hangs open, empty now.
c1.hatch_shut: A little hatch under the clock face. It doesn't budge.
c1.intro: You wake in a lakeside cottage. The lamp is out, the clock has stopped, and the goldfish is staring at you.
c1.jar_frantic: A moth beats itself against the glass of the jar, frantic. It would calm down if there were a light to look at.
c1.jar_open: You lift the lid. The moth sits very still, then rises, and the room tilts away from you.
c1.lake_shapes: Now the moth hangs over the glass, four pale shapes surface in the dark water, upside down: an eye, a moon, a fish, a bell.
c1.lake_still: The lake is perfectly still. Not a ripple. A single pinprick of light sits on the horizon, far off. It is out.
c1.lantern_burning: It burns steadily in the window. You'll take it with you when you go.
c1.lantern_lit: The candle gives up its flame. The lantern burns, small and steady.
c1.lantern_oiled: You fill the lantern. The wick drinks greedily.
c1.lantern_placed: You set the lantern in the window. Far out on the lake, a pinprick of light answers it.
c1.lantern_take: A storm lantern, cold and dry. You take it.
c1.leave: You step out onto the jetty, the lantern swinging in your hand. The door shuts behind you.
c1.leave_missing.chart: You can't leave without the chart of the lake. Something in you is certain.
c1.leave_missing.oar: You can't leave without the oar. You'll be rowing, one way or another.
c1.leave_missing.ticket: There was a ticket in the coat. Take it before you go. It's dated for a day that hasn't come.
c1.lockbox: A lock with four dials. Each one shows a different shape.
c1.mat_lift: You lift the corner of the doormat. Something is tucked beneath it: a scrap of paper.
c1.match_take: A single match, kept where only the clock could keep it.
c1.mirror.1: Your reflection nods. A moment after you do.
c1.mirror.2: It runs late again. Half a second, no more, like an echo that has to run to catch you.
c1.mirror.3: It catches up, out of breath, and holds something out to you through the glass: a corner of a photograph.
c1.mirror.4: It stands very still now. Waiting, perhaps.
c1.moth_free: The moth circles the flame, content.
c1.moth_w: The moth presses itself against the glass, drawn to the lantern.
c1.moth_window: The moth drifts to the lantern in the window and settles there, trembling in the warmth.
c1.note_take: A note, in your own handwriting, signed with a single initial: R.
c1.oar_take: A good ash oar, worn smooth at the grip. You take it.
c1.oil_take: A bottle of lamp oil. You take it.
c1.painting_dark: The painting tells you nothing. It's too dark to make out more than smears of paint.
c1.painting_lit: In the candlelight the picture swims up out of the dark: a lake, a far lighthouse, four floats in a row, a heron at the edge.
c1.painting_seen: Four floats across still water. Each one has its own colour, and its own pattern.
c1.pell_chat.1: "I'm only a fish," says Pell. "A fish who sees everything. It's not the same thing as helping."
c1.pell_chat.2: "Don't look at me. The clock is on the other wall."
c1.pell_chat.3: "It's very quiet, isn't it? The lake hasn't moved in years."
c1.pell_chat.5: "Light things. It's what we do here."
c1.pell_chat.6: Pell blows a bubble, regards it, and lets it go.
c1.pell_clock: "Both hands pointed straight at me. I was there, you know. Make of that what you will."
c1.pell_fed: Pell falls on the flakes with enormous dignity, and no dignity at all. When he's done he looks up. "Both hands pointed straight at me," he says.
c1.pell_full: Pell hasn't room for another flake. He tells you so, in bubbles.
c1.pell_hungry: The goldfish watches you with one oddly human eye, and then, pointedly, at his empty surface.
c1.photo: A photograph of this very room. Someone is standing in it, back to the camera, exactly where you are standing now.
c1.plaque: A pike, mounted on a plaque. Its glass eye holds yours a moment longer than it should.
c1.pocket_empty: Empty now. Just lint and the smell of rain.
c1.pocket_l: Your fingers find paper in the left pocket: a ferry ticket.
c1.pocket_r: In the right pocket, cold against your fingertips: a brass key.
c1.sill_unlit: A dark lantern in a window is only a lantern. It needs a flame first.
c1.sorry: Burned letters. One word survived the fire.
c1.ticket_take: A ferry ticket. Dated tomorrow. You take it, though you couldn't say why.
c2.bell_ring: You tap the boat's brass bell. It gives one bright note that goes out across the water and doesn't come back.
c2.bottle_look: A ship in a bottle: a tiny ferry on painted waves. Its sail has caught something. It twitches.
c2.bottle_open: The cork pops. The moth shakes out its wings and lifts from the sail, and the room tilts away from you.
c2.bow_lamp_lit: The moth drifts out through the door, across the boathouse, and into the boat's bow lamp. The lamp catches.
c2.catch_have: You've a fish already. One is enough for anyone.
c2.catch_miss: The net comes up empty, dripping. Too early, or too late.
c2.catch_nonet: You haven't anything to put in the water.
c2.chain_open: The padlock snaps open. The chain falls away from the bow ring and pools on the ground.
c2.chain_slack: The chain lies slack on the ground.
c2.cork_stuck: The cork is jammed in the neck, sealed with old wax. You'd need something to pull it.
c2.corkscrew_take: A corkscrew. The kind a person keeps for bottles, and for no other reason.
c2.crank_done: The winch has done its work.
c2.crank_spins: The crank turns freely and does nothing. The gears aren't all there.
c2.crate_open: You pry the lid off the crate. Inside, packed in straw, a big brass gear.
c2.drum_look: A big wooden drum wound with rope. The rope runs down through the floor, toward the boat.
c2.fish_caught: The net comes up heavy: a small silver fish, thrashing. Pell, in his jar, is deeply offended.
c2.gap_look: Through the gap in the planks, the water below. Something silver passes across it now and then.
c2.gear_placed: The gear slips over the peg and sits snug.
c2.gear_removed: You lift the gear back off its peg.
c2.gear_take: A brass gear, heavier than it looks. You take it.
c2.gears_gap: The crank turns a gear, but its teeth miss the next one's: there's a gap between them. The drum doesn't move.
c2.gears_jam: The teeth grind against each other and jam: the gears are crowded too close. The drum doesn't move.
c2.heron_aside_look: The heron has stepped aside and is watching the water. It has not forgotten you.
c2.heron_fed1: The heron takes the fish in one neat motion, and walks, very slowly, to the next piling. It leaves the oar. It doesn't say thank you. It wouldn't.
c2.heron_fed2: The heron swallows the second fish, opens its wings, and is gone into the fog. A moment later it is back on the third piling, something pale held in its beak.
c2.heron_frag_look: The heron holds something pale in its beak, with the air of a bird who knows exactly what it has.
c2.heron_full: The heron regards the fish, then you. It has had enough of fish for one night.
c2.heron_look: The heron stands guard over a second oar, leaning against the piling. It looks at you with total patience, and at your pockets with more.
c2.hole_look: A ragged hole, the size of a dinner plate, stove into the hull. The lake would find it in a moment.
c2.hook_bare: An iron hook in the beam. A lantern would hang well from it.
c2.hull_ok: The patch has taken hold. The hull is sound.
c2.hull_patched: You press the patch over the hole. The tar bites into the wood, black and smooth. It will hold.
c2.intro: Fog. A jetty runs out into water that does not move. On a piling at its end stands a heron you could swear was in a painting an hour ago.
c2.jar_take: A pickle jar, and in it, with great dignity, Pell. "I've decided to come," he says. "Don't argue. Whoever heard of a lighthouse without a fish?" He rides in the crook of your arm from now on.
c2.lamp_cold: The boat's bow lamp is cold, glass and empty.
c2.lamp_lit: The moth sits in the lamp, glowing. The bow lamp burns.
c2.lantern_hung.back: You hang the lantern. The back wall comes up out of the dark; the rest of the boathouse stays black.
c2.lantern_hung.left: You hang the lantern. The workbench wall comes up out of the dark; the rest of the boathouse stays black.
c2.lantern_hung.right: You hang the lantern. The slip and the boat come up out of the dark; the rest of the boathouse stays black.
c2.lantern_take: You lift the lantern off its hook. The wall slides back into the dark.
c2.launch: You push off from the slip. The lamp swings, the oars dip, and the boathouse falls away behind you into the fog.
c2.launch_chain: The boat is chained to its post. It's not going anywhere.
c2.launch_cradle: The boat is still sitting on its cradle, high and dry. It needs to be in the water first; there's a winch for that.
c2.launch_hull: Not with a hole in the hull. The lake is waiting for you to forget it.
c2.launch_jar: You can't go without Pell. He's still on the workbench, making his feelings known.
c2.launch_lamp: It's dark out there. The bow lamp needs a light.
c2.launch_net: The net. You'll want the net out there; something tells you so.
c2.launch_oars: A boat wants two oars, set in its oarlocks.
c2.lock_look: A padlock with three number wheels, hanging from the chain.
c2.net_look: A fishing net, wound into a knot. A float at one end, a weight at the other, and a great deal of rope between that doesn't go where it should.
c2.net_look_done: The net lies straight, float to weight.
c2.net_take: A net, sound, if a little frayed. You take it.
c2.net_untangled: The last knot gives. The rope runs clear, float to weight, and the net falls open.
c2.oar2_take: The second oar: the pair of the one you carry. You take it.
c2.oar_placed: The oar slides into the oarlock, a perfect fit.
c2.oarlock_full: There's an oar in there already.
c2.patch_first: You need to make a patch of it first: tar soaks into the rag.
c2.patch_made: You press the soft tar into the rag and fold it. A patch, thick and black and sticky.
c2.peg_taken: There's a gear on that peg already.
c2.plank_hollow: One floorboard sounds different under your knuckles. Hollow.
c2.plank_lift: The board lifts, puffing dust. Underneath, something pale is wedged in the dark.
c2.rag_burn: A rag and a flame. A very bad idea, in a wooden boathouse.
c2.rag_take: A clean, dry rag, folded square.
c2.tackle_look: A tackle box: hooks, lead weights, a spool of line.
c2.tar_cold: A pot of tar, cold and hard as a plank. It would need some warmth.
c2.tar_empty: You've taken all the tar you can carry.
c2.tar_soft: The lantern's warmth has softened the tar. You scoop a lump of it.
c2.tide_420: At 04:20 the water stood at 172 cm.
c2.tide_other: At {0}, the water stood at {1} cm. Nothing about that hour rings a bell.
c2.winch_turns: Gear bites gear. The drum turns, the rope pays out, and the boat Agnes slides down the slip with a long, wet sigh into the black water.
c3.arrive.buoy: A bell buoy leans in the water, ringing a slow rhythm you can feel through the boards.
c3.arrive.deep: The water goes black and very still. The boat slows to a stop, and the oars bite nothing.
c3.arrive.green: A green float, dotted, bobbing slightly at its mooring.
c3.arrive.landing: The far light rises out of the fog, its landing stage grey with salt.
c3.arrive.pale: A pale float, patterned in chevrons, quiet as a ghost.
c3.arrive.red: A float rides low in the water, striped red. You bring the boat alongside it.
c3.arrive.reeds: Reeds, thick and dry, rattling though there is no wind.
c3.arrive.tree: A drowned tree stands out of the water, bare and grey. Something glints, high in its branches.
c3.arrive.yellow: A plain yellow float, nodding to itself.
c3.bell_answered: Long, short, short, long. The buoy falls silent. Then, far away, the fog begins to lift.
c3.bell_hint: The boat's bell hangs on its post. Hold it for a long note, tap it for a short one.
c3.bell_nothing: A fine rhythm. Nothing out here answers it.
c3.bell_wrong: The bell rings out, and the buoy waits. That wasn't its rhythm.
c3.boat_wont_move: The oars bite water that isn't there. The boat will not move. Something below is holding it.
c3.bottle_high: A bottle is wedged in the fork of the branches, far out of reach of an oar. You'd need something that scoops.
c3.bottle_net: You swing the net up into the branches and the bottle drops into it. Inside is a folded note.
c3.buoy_rings: The buoy rings, over and over, in a pattern: long, short, short, long. Ripples spread from it in the same rhythm.
c3.channel_open: The fourth chime rings out across the lake. The water ahead deepens, dark and clear, and a channel opens through the shallows.
c3.chart_edge: The fog at the edge of the chart is a wall. You turn the boat back.
c3.chart_look: The chart of the lake, a five-by-five grid. A spot is circled in red.
c3.chart_tap: You can row straight back to places you've been and remember: the floats, the tree, the buoy, the reeds.
c3.compass_look: A brass compass. Its card is loose, free to be turned by hand.
c3.compass_set: The card swings true: S under the stern, N over the bow. The chart's grid takes on headings, and the oars feel like oars again.
c3.deep_arrive: The water is perfectly still and perfectly black. A spot on the chart is circled in red, and this is it.
c3.deep_look: The water looks like a polished stone.
c3.down_after: The moth climbs up through the water and settles on your lantern, shaking itself dry. The boat moves, as if it had only been waiting to be released.
c3.down_done: You've seen enough of what lies down there.
c3.down_nothing: Black water, and your own faint shape in it. You remember the chart's warning and look away.
c3.down_see: Far below, a ferry lies on the bottom of the lake with all its lights still burning. And a hand, a pale one, opens toward the surface, and lets something go.
c3.float_again: You've touched that one already. The chime sounds once more, as if to be sure.
c3.float_done: The float nods. Its work is done.
c3.float_ok.1: A faint chime from somewhere below the water, like a glass struck once. Something is pleased.
c3.float_ok.2: Another chime, a little higher. The way opens, a little.
c3.float_ok.3: A third chime. Only one float remains.
c3.float_wrong: No chime. The channel closes behind you, and the current takes the boat and sets it back, one cell, to where you were.
c3.fog_wall: Ahead, the fog is thick as a wall. The light is somewhere behind it, and not yet ready.
c3.heron_gives: The heron, standing on the drowned ferry's mast in the middle of the open lake, regards you, shifts its weight, and lets something pale fall from its beak into the boat.
c3.intro: The boat slides out of the boathouse and the fog closes behind it. Only one thing holds still: the cottage window you lit, small and warm, astern.
c3.landing_arrive: The post is stout and old. A throw, and the boat is tied.
c3.lantern_look: Your lantern burns on its hook, a small warm island in the grey.
c3.line_look: A coil of mooring line, stiff with salt.
c3.moor_miss: The line falls short, and slaps the water. You haul it in and try again.
c3.moor_pell: "Aren't you forgetting something?" says Pell. "I haven't been in the lake yet." (Open the deck, and Pell's jar.)
c3.moored: The loop drops over the post and pulls tight. The boat swings in against the stage, and stops.
c3.no_chart: You have no chart to spread out.
c3.no_heading: You dip the oars and the boat turns lazily on the spot. Without a heading, in this fog, you could row in circles until morning.
c3.pell_asks: Pell presses his face to the glass. "Let me into the lake. Just for a moment. I'll come straight back, I promise. There's something down there that I want to find." He looks at you with his one human eye. (Tip the jar to let him go.)
c3.pell_chat.1: "I do hope you know where we're going," says Pell.
c3.pell_chat.2: "Don't look at me. I'm a fish. We don't navigate, we drift."
c3.pell_chat.3: "That water looks lovely. Not that I'd know."
c3.pell_chat.4: "Fog. My favourite weather. It hides things."
c3.pell_chat.5: "I used to know someone who rowed this lake every night."
c3.pell_chat.6: "Don't look down, the chart says. I'd listen to the chart."
c3.pell_dives: You tip the jar over the side. Pell slips into the dark water like a coin, and is gone.
c3.pell_returns: A flash of orange, and Pell is back in the jar with something in his mouth: a heavy iron key. "I told you," he says, "just a moment."
c3.post_look: A landing post, black with tar and salt.
c3.reeds_look: A tangle of dry reeds. Something glass shows low among the stems.
c3.row.1: Stroke, and another. The boat slides on through the fog.
c3.row.2: The oars dip and lift. Drops fall from the blades like slow clocks.
c3.row.3: The fog presses in, soft and close. Nothing but water.
c3.row.4: A stroke. Another. The lantern light swings on the water.
c3.row.5: The lake doesn't move. The boat is the only thing that does.
c3.row.6: Fog, and water, and the sound of your own breathing.
c3.shoal: The water shoals under the keel. The boat grinds to a halt and the current nudges you back. There must be a marked way through.
c3.teleport: You row back along the remembered way.
c3.tree_look: The branches are dead and bleached, and very high.
c4.cal_lift: A page of the calendar, with a date circled in red. You lift it, and look underneath.
c4.cal_now: The calendar is faded to nothing, one corner torn away. The month can still be made out, just.
c4.chain_break: The chain that carries the rotation weight has snapped, its last link bent open.
c4.chain_fit: You fit the spare chain, link by link. It takes the weight with a long metallic sigh. The lens can turn again.
c4.chain_take: A length of chain from the drawer: strong, well oiled, a spare. You take it.
c4.chain_then: In the past, the chain is whole. The break is in the present.
c4.chair_empty: The watch chair stands empty and cold, dust on its seat.
c4.door_locked: A tall door, black with salt and rain. The lock is old and heavy, and the keyhole is the shape of a long iron key.
c4.door_unlocked: The key turns with a groan of old iron. The door swings inward onto the cold dark of the lighthouse.
c4.drawer_rust: The drawer is rusted shut, welded into its frame. Not even a crowbar would move it.
c4.enter: Inside: cold stone, the smell of rain and rust, and a stair winding up into the dark.
c4.era_now: Now: cold and quiet, the rain steady on the stone.
c4.era_rules: The world slides like a slide changing in a lantern: the same room, a different night. A rule settles in you without a word: what you carry crosses with you.
c4.era_then: Then: warm and loud, the storm at the windows, the lamp burning low.
c4.intro: The far light stands on its rock, grey with rain. The door is tall, and deeply locked. "Salt," says Pell, sniffing. "And something older than salt."
c4.lake_still: And the water, which has not moved for years, goes perfectly still. Not a ripple. As though the whole lake were holding its breath.
c4.lamp_lit: You touch the lantern's flame to the wick. It catches, steady and bright. The oil climbs, the chain turns, and the lens gathers the light and flings it out across the lake in one long sweep.
c4.lamp_need_chain: The lens won't turn: the chain that carries its weight is broken.
c4.lamp_need_lens: A flame now would only scatter in the prisms. The lens isn't aligned.
c4.lamp_need_oil: The wick is dry. The oil hasn't reached it yet.
c4.lamp_need_past: Something in the past still lies unfinished. Not yet.
c4.lamp_then: In the past, the lamp is low but burning. It's the present's lamp that is dark.
c4.lens_aligned: The beam, from the lamp, wheels once through the prisms and leaves by the seaward window, straight and bright.
c4.log_again: The page says what it said: the valve settings for the night, and the line that stops in the middle of a word.
c4.log_read: In the lamplight, the page for that night is whole. The writing is yours. There are valve settings, and a line that stops in the middle of a word.
c4.log_torn: The logbook lies open on the desk. The page for that night has been torn out, leaving a ragged stub. Whatever it said, the present has lost it.
c4.oil_flows: The last valve clicks home. Far above, brass pipes shudder, and oil begins to climb toward the lamp.
c4.oilcan_take: An oilcan, long-spouted and half full. In the lamplight of that night it's right where it always was. You take it.
c4.rule_persist: Something you moved in the past stays moved in the present. The past can be visited, but not undone.
c4.shelf_look: Shelves of the keeper's stores: jars, crates, rope. All of it long past use.
c4.shelf_ring: On the middle shelf there's a clean ring in the dust, as if something that stood here for years has been lifted away.
c4.sleeper_420: The second hand passes the twelve. 4:20. The lamp gutters, and goes out.
c4.sleeper_after: The room holds its breath. You know the handwriting. You know the chair. You know who fell asleep, and who left the lamp to burn dry.
c4.sleeper_again: The sleeper doesn't stir. You have seen enough.
c4.sleeper_face: The sleeper stirs, and turns toward you. It has your face.
c4.sleeper_watch: In the chair by the window, someone sleeps, head on their arm. You take out the watch and hold it up. 4:19.
c4.stem_take: Under a litter of nails and washers: a small brass winding stem.
c4.step_hollow: One step sounds different under your boot. Hollow.
c4.step_lift: You pry the step up. Under it, wedged in the dark, something pale.
c4.valve_board: Three brass valves set in a board, each marked 0 to 9. The oil for the great lamp runs through them.
c4.valve_oiled: You work oil into the seized valve until it creaks, and gives, and turns. In the past, the oil sinks into the brass. In the present, the same valve will turn.
c4.valve_oiled_already: The valve has been oiled, and turns freely.
c4.valve_seized: The valve won't turn. It's rusted solid, welded by years of salt air. Nothing here will free it.
c4.valves_locked: The valves are set. Somewhere above, oil begins to climb.
c4.valves_right_dry: The numbers are right, but nothing comes. The seized valve has a long way yet to go.
c4.watch_fixed: You slide the stem home and wind it. The watch ticks once, twice, and the room shivers. (The watch will carry you between Then and Now: press the watch at the top left, or T.)
c4.watch_take: A pocket watch, stopped at 4:19. The winding stem is missing, and the glass is cracked.
c4.wick_look: The lamp's wick, black and dry, waiting for a flame.
c5.armchair_b: The armchair, reflected. Whatever warmth lives in it lives Above.
c5.ash_already: The ash lies in the grate already.
c5.ash_placed: You scatter the ash across the bars. It lies there, grey and soft.
c5.ash_take: A handful of ash: cold, fine, and very light. It is all that's left of a great many letters.
c5.backfire: You hold the lantern to the ash, and the fire runs backwards. The ash gathers, glows, draws itself up into flame, and the flame falls inward, into paper.
c5.books_above: Four books stand out from the others. Their order feels like someone else's.
c5.books_below: Four books stand out from the others. Reflected, they read right to left.
c5.books_done: The last book slides into place. Behind the shelf, something drops, small and heavy, into your hand: a ticket punch.
c5.books_sorted: Red stripes, green dots, pale chevrons, plain yellow: Above, exactly the painting's order.
c5.bowl_dry: The bowl is dry, and has been for a very long time.
c5.bowl_empty: Below, Pell's bowl stands empty. The water is perfectly clear. It's waiting for someone.
c5.bowl_pell: Pell drifts in his own bowl at last, and says nothing, and looks happy.
c5.cabinet: The cabinet is shut and empty.
c5.candle: The candle stub, burned to the saucer.
c5.chair_seat: The seat is warm, and glowing softly where the moth rests.
c5.clock_done: The face swings open. Inside, folded very small: a page torn from the logbook, and a ferry timetable. Above, in the dust, the clock reads 4:20.
c5.clock_set_hint: The hands tick round. Above, the clock follows, turned around: whatever you set here, it shows the other way.
c5.coat: The coat hangs with its pockets empty. Everything it held has gone on ahead of you.
c5.cross_down: You touch the glass, and sink through.
c5.cross_first: You touch the glass. It gives, cool as water, and you step through.
c5.cross_up: You touch the glass, and rise, through the cold, into the dusty light.
c5.desk: The desk. Dust has settled over everything except one rectangle where the chart used to lie.
c5.door: The door is shut. It opens on a jetty you've already left.
c5.drawer: The drawer is empty. You took everything it had to give.
c5.fish_below: A tiny fish beside the four, as above. Only the mechanism is turned around.
c5.grate_b: A bare hearth. Nothing here has ever burned. Everything here has always been about to.
c5.grate_nothing: A flame to an empty hearth. Nothing to burn, nothing to unburn.
c5.hatch_shut: A small hatch under the clock face. It doesn't budge.
c5.intro: You wake in the cottage, dusty and silent. Above, the far light you lit sweeps its slow beam across the lake, and down, through the water, and in at the window. In the mirror on the door wall, your reflection is waiting for you.
c5.letter_take: The letter. Whole. In your own hand. You read it, and for the first time, you say it, out loud: you are sorry.
c5.letter_whole: The fire folds itself away into the grate, and lying on the bars, whole, is a letter you never sent.
c5.logpage_take: The torn page from the logbook, folded very small. You unfold it.
c5.mat: RETURN, says the mat. You step around it.
c5.moth_choice: The last moth rests in the warm armchair, trembling a little. It is yours to keep, or to let go.
c5.moth_unheard: The moth stirs, but doesn't rise. There is someone who hasn't heard it yet.
c5.moth_unsaid: The moth stirs, but doesn't rise. There is something you haven't said.
c5.painting: The painting is too dark to read. It doesn't need reading any more.
c5.pell_last: "I always knew it was you," says Pell. "I just wanted you to say it."
c5.pell_poured: You pour Pell out into the bowl. He swirls once, twice, and settles at the bottom, enormous with dignity.
c5.photo_turned: In the reflection, the figure in the photograph has turned around, and is looking out at you.
c5.plaque_moved: The plaque swings aside on a hinge you hadn't noticed. Behind it, in the dark gap, something pale. Its mirror image reads: SHE NEVER ASKED.
c5.punch_ready: You set the ticket in the punch. A grid of holes waits to be pressed: an hour, and a minute.
c5.punch_take: A small steel ticket punch, bright and cold. You take it.
c5.sill: The sill where the lantern burned. A ring in the dust now.
c5.ticket_look: A ferry ticket, one crossing. A grid of holes waits to be punched.
c5.ticket_valid: The punch bites. The ticket is valid now: dated today, for the last crossing. And Above, the armchair turns slowly to face you.
c5.ticket_wrong: The punch clicks, and the ticket takes the holes, and shrugs. Wrong. A fresh blank slides into place: the lake forgives.
c5.timetable_take: A ferry timetable, soft with age. You unfold it.
c5.window: The far light turns across the water, and its beam comes down through the lake and the glass, onto the floor.
cap.ferry_horn: a ferry horn, low and long
cap.ripple: water ripples, for the first time
cap.throw: a line whips through the air
chapter.1.title: The Keeper's Room
chapter.2.title: The Boathouse
chapter.3.title: The Crossing
chapter.4.title: The Far Light
chapter.5.title: Still Water
choice.release: Release it into the far light
choice.title: The last moth
clock.locked: The hands are fixed now. Whatever the clock was holding has been let go.
combine.gear_m.gear_l: The gears' teeth fit nicely together, but it takes a winch to do something with them.
combine.gear_s.gear_m: The gears' teeth fit nicely together, but it takes a winch to do something with them.
combine.generic.1: Those two have nothing to say to each other.
combine.generic.3: You turn them over in your hands. No.
combine.key.lantern: The key and the lantern have nothing to do with each other.
combine.lantern.candle_lit: The wick drinks nothing. The lantern is dry. It needs oil before it can use your flame.
combine.net.small_fish: The fish is quite finished with the net.
combine.oil.candle_lit: Fire and lamp oil, without a lantern in between. No.
combine.oilcan.chain: The chain is already well oiled.
dials.locked: The dials are set. The lock has done its work.
end.A.1: You open your hand. The last moth rises, and goes toward the light.
end.A.2: It reaches the far light, and the far light holds it, and burns a little brighter.
end.A.3: And dawn comes. For the first time in years, a breath of wind crosses the lake, and the water ripples.
end.A.4: An empty ferry docks at the jetty.
end.A.5: The ticket in your hand is dated today.
end.A.sub: You let it go. The lake begins to move.
end.A.title: Morning
end.B.1: You close the jar. The moth is very still.
end.B.2: The room resets itself around you, patiently, like a held breath let out.
end.B.3: You wake in the Keeper's Room. The lamp is out. The clock has stopped.
end.B.4: Your reflection arrives, a second late.
end.B.sub: You kept the light. The room begins again.
end.B.title: Still Water
end.C.1: You find the bell, and you ring it.
end.C.2: And the photograph, in your hands, comes together: two people on a ferry deck, shoulder to shoulder, laughing.
end.C.4: A light, a second light, small and warm, crosses the water toward the jetty.
end.C.sub: You were heard. Two lights cross the water.
end.C.title: Two Lights
frag.get: A fragment of a photograph. ({0} of 10)
game.tagline: Relight the lights. Recover five memories. Find out why the lamp went out at 4:20.
game.title: Still Water
hint.1.1.2: The coat has two pockets. Try both.
hint.1.1.3: The brass key is in the right pocket.
hint.1.10.1: Now that the moth is at the window, look out at the lake.
hint.1.10.2: Four shapes in the water, upside down. The door has four dials.
hint.1.10.3: Eye, moon, fish, bell: set the dials in that order, left to right.
hint.1.2.2: Under the window: a brass-rimmed keyhole.
hint.1.2.3: Use the key on the desk drawer, under the window.
hint.1.3.1: Someone in this room is hungry.
hint.1.3.2: The tin from the drawer. The bowl is on the west wall.
hint.1.3.3: Use the fish food on the bowl, then speak to him.
hint.1.4.1: Clocks. Never trust a stopped one.
hint.1.4.2: There's something tiny engraved on that clock face. Near the four.
hint.1.4.3: Both hands on the fish. Twenty past four. Honestly.
hint.1.5.1: You got something out of that clock. Fire needs a flame.
hint.1.5.2: A candle stub on the mantel, right of the clock.
hint.1.5.3: Use the match on the candle.
hint.1.6.1: The painting tells you nothing in the dark.
hint.1.6.2: Take the burning candle. Light helps a painting.
hint.1.6.3: Pick up the lit candle and hold it to the painting.
hint.1.7.1: Four books on the shelf. Four floats in the painting.
hint.1.7.2: Put the books in the order of the floats, left to right. Match the patterns, not just the colours.
hint.1.7.3: Red stripes, green dots, pale chevrons, plain yellow. Swap them until they stand that way.
hint.1.8.1: The lantern is dry. Something in the cabinet isn't.
hint.1.8.2: Oil first, then a flame, then a window.
hint.1.8.3: Combine oil with the lantern, then the lit candle with the lantern, then use it on the windowsill.
hint.1.9.1: That moth has been banging on its jar all evening.
hint.1.9.2: It will calm down now there's a light burning.
hint.1.9.3: Open the jar on the desk.
hint.2.1.1: It's very dark in there, and you carry the only light.
hint.2.1.2: There are iron hooks high on three of the walls. A lantern hangs well from a hook.
hint.2.1.3: Use the lit lantern on a hook. The wall it hangs on lights up, and the others stay dark.
hint.2.2.1: The boat is chained, and the lock has three wheels.
hint.2.2.2: What does the tide table say about the hour the clock stopped?
hint.2.2.3: Find 04:20 on the tide table, on the noticeboard wall. The level is 172. Set the wheels to 1, 7, 2.
hint.2.3.1: There's a hole in the hull.
hint.2.3.2: A rag and some warm tar make a patch. The tar is on the workbench, the rag is in the tackle box.
hint.2.3.3: Hang the lantern near the tar to warm it. Take the tar and combine it with the rag, then use the patch on the hole.
hint.2.4.1: That net is in a state.
hint.2.4.2: Turn the knot tiles until one rope runs from the float to the weight.
hint.2.4.3: Across the top-left tile, then turn down; at the middle, turn right; then down; then right again, out of the bottom-right tile.
hint.2.5.1: Something silver swims under the jetty.
hint.2.5.2: There's a gap in the planks of the jetty, and now you have a net.
hint.2.5.3: Go to the gap, and click when the silver shadow is under the lit patch of water.
hint.2.6.3: Give the small fish to the heron on the piling at the end of the jetty.
hint.2.7.1: That winch isn't going to turn itself.
hint.2.7.2: Three gears are scattered about the boathouse. The pegs are set at different distances.
hint.2.7.3: Small gear on the crank peg, middle gear in the middle, large gear on the drum peg. Then turn the crank.
hint.2.8.1: A moth is caught in the bottle. Pell would call it a hostage.
hint.2.8.2: The cork is stuck. The tackle box has something for corks.
hint.2.8.3: Use the corkscrew on the bottle on the workbench wall.
hint.2.9.2: Two oars in the oarlocks, the lamp lit, the hole patched, the chain off, Pell on board.
hint.2.9.3: Put both oars into the boat's oarlocks, then push off.
hint.3.1.1: The compass card spins loose. The chart's margin says something about the stern.
hint.3.1.2: The cottage window you lit is due south, behind you, astern.
hint.3.1.3: In the compass, turn the card until the S points down, toward the stern.
hint.3.2.1: Four floats mark the way through the shallows. You have seen them before.
hint.3.2.2: The painting in the cottage showed them in an order. The notebook remembers. Touch each float in that order.
hint.3.2.3: Red first: two strokes west, one north of the start. Then green: one north, one east. Then pale: two east. Then yellow: two south.
hint.3.3.1: A bottle is caught in a tree.
hint.3.3.2: You've something that scoops things out of water, and a drowned tree to the east of the start, near the shore.
hint.3.3.3: Row to the drowned tree and use the net on the bottle.
hint.3.4.1: The buoy keeps a rhythm. Go and listen to it.
hint.3.4.2: Long, short, short, long. The ripples show it too. Answer on the boat's bell, at the stern.
hint.3.4.3: Beyond the shallows, east of the deep: the bell buoy. Ring the boat's bell, holding for long and tapping for short: long, short, short, long.
hint.3.5.1: Pell has been trying to say something.
hint.3.5.2: He'd like out of the jar, just for a moment.
hint.3.5.3: Open the deck and click Pell's jar, twice, to let him over the side.
hint.3.6.1: The chart has a circled spot, and a warning.
hint.3.6.2: The boat won't move at the circled spot. Do what the chart tells you not to.
hint.3.6.3: Row to the circled spot, then tap the water beside the boat at the bottom of the screen: look down.
hint.3.7.1: The far light's landing is waiting.
hint.3.7.2: It's north of the circled spot, at the top middle of the chart.
hint.3.7.3: Row to the landing, go up to the post, and throw the mooring line over it.
hint.4.1.1: The door is locked, and Pell went to some trouble for a key.
hint.4.1.2: The key Pell brought up from the lake.
hint.4.1.3: Use the lighthouse key on the door's lock.
hint.4.2.1: That pocket watch is stopped, and incomplete.
hint.4.2.2: A winding stem. A tin in the store room, among the small things.
hint.4.2.3: Open the tin in the store room (the shelf on the left), take the stem and combine it with the watch from the quarters.
hint.4.3.1: The logbook has something to say about that night.
hint.4.3.2: The logbook is on the desk in the watch room. In the present, the page is torn out. Use the watch.
hint.4.3.3: Go to Then, open the logbook, and read the page: valve settings 3, 1, 4.
hint.4.4.1: Oil has to reach the lamp, and valves are in the way.
hint.4.4.2: The valves in the watch room: set them from the log, and free the seized one with oil. The oilcan was in the store room. Then.
hint.4.4.3: Take the oilcan in Then, oil the middle valve, then set the valves to 3, 1, 4.
hint.4.5.1: A spare chain would be useful. There's a drawer.
hint.4.5.2: The drawer in the quarters is rusted shut in Now. It wasn't always.
hint.4.5.3: In Then, open the drawer and take the chain. In Now, fit it to the chain mechanism in the lamp room.
hint.4.6.1: The lens is a puzzle of mirrors.
hint.4.6.2: The beam starts at the left and must leave by the sea window, at the top right.
hint.4.6.3: Turn the panels until the beam zigzags out at the top right.
hint.4.7.1: The chair in the watch room is not as empty as it looks.
hint.4.7.2: In Then, look at the figure in the chair. Use the watch to see the minute.
hint.4.7.3: In Then, open the chair in the watch room and watch the clock tick to 4:20.
hint.4.8.2: A flame, to the wick, in the present.
hint.4.8.3: In Now, use the lit lantern on the wick in the lamp room.
hint.5.1.1: Your reflection has been waiting a long time.
hint.5.1.2: The mirror on the door wall.
hint.5.1.3: Open the mirror on the door wall (the one with the gilt frame) and touch the glass.
hint.5.2.2: For the clock Above to read what it read on the night, the clock Below has to read the mirror of it.
hint.5.2.3: Set the clock Below to 7:40. Above it will read 4:20.
hint.5.3.2: Take the ash from the grate Above. Carry it down, and put it in the grate Below, and light it.
hint.5.3.3: Take the ash Above; Below, use it on the grate, then light it with the lantern.
hint.5.4.1: The books Below are in a reflection of the order you want.
hint.5.4.2: Arrange them so that Above they read in the painting's order: red, green, pale, yellow, left to right.
hint.5.4.3: Below, swap the books until reading right to left they read red stripes, green dots, pale chevrons, plain yellow.
hint.5.5.2: You have Pell with you. He's in a pickle jar.
hint.5.5.3: Below, use Pell's jar on the empty bowl.
hint.5.6.1: A ticket, a punch, and a timetable.
hint.5.6.2: The timetable lists Tomas's last crossing. The punch makes it valid.
hint.5.6.3: Combine the ticket with the punch, and punch 4:30: hour 4, minute 30.
hint.5.7.1: The last moth rests in the warm armchair.
hint.5.7.2: Three things were left unsaid, unheard, undone. When they're done, the chair turns.
hint.5.7.3: Touch the moth in the armchair, and choose.
hint.none: Nothing is stuck. Look around, then look again.
hintr.1.1.2: R. — a coat has two pockets. Check them both.
hintr.1.2.1: R. — the desk has a drawer. Under the window.
hintr.1.2.2: R. — brass-rimmed keyhole. You know the one.
hintr.1.2.3: R. — the key from the coat, in the drawer.
hintr.1.3.1: R. — you were told to feed the fish.
hintr.1.3.2: R. — the tin from the drawer; the bowl on the west wall.
hintr.1.3.3: R. — the food on the bowl. Then talk to him.
item.ash.desc: A handful of fine grey ash from the grate.
item.ash.name: Ash
item.candle_lit.desc: A stub of candle on its saucer. The flame leans away from your breath.
item.candle_lit.name: Lit candle
item.chain.desc: A length of strong, well-oiled chain.
item.chain.name: Spare chain
item.chart.desc: A chart of the lake on a five-by-five grid. A spot is circled in red. Something is written in the margin.
item.chart.name: Chart of the lake
item.chart.text:
STERN TO HOME.
DO NOT LOOK DOWN.
item.corkscrew.desc: A corkscrew, brass and well worn.
item.corkscrew.name: Corkscrew
item.food.desc: A tin of flakes. The label is a drawing of a very pleased fish.
item.food.name: Fish food
item.gear_l.desc: A large brass gear, wide as a dinner plate.
item.gear_l.name: Large gear
item.gear_m.desc: A medium brass gear, heavier than it looks.
item.gear_m.name: Middle gear
item.gear_s.desc: A small brass gear. The sort of thing that wants a peg.
item.gear_s.name: Small gear
item.key.desc: Heavy, worn, warm from the pocket it came out of.
item.key.name: Brass key
item.lantern.desc: A storm lantern. Cold, dry, and not much use like this.
item.lantern.name: Lantern
item.lantern_lit.desc: A storm lantern, burning small and steady. You can carry the light with you.
item.lantern_lit.name: Lantern (lit)
item.lantern_oil.desc: The lantern, filled with oil. It needs a flame.
item.lantern_oil.name: Lantern (filled)
item.letter.desc: A letter to Tomas, unburned: whole, in your own hand.
item.letter.name: Ruth's letter
item.letter.text:
Tomas,

You asked me to come, and I said no, and then I said worse. I meant none of it. I was afraid: of the water, of leaving the light, of being someone who wasn't the keeper.

I'm sorry. I'm sorry I let you go out in that.

Come home. I'll keep the lamp lit. I'll keep it lit all night.

— Ruth
item.lhkey.desc: A long iron key, wet from the lake. Pell fetched it from the deep.
item.lhkey.name: Lighthouse key
item.logpage.desc: The page that was torn from the log on the night of the storm.
item.logpage.name: Logbook page
item.logpage.text:
04:15. Storm easing a little. Lamp low but holding.
I'll close my eyes for a minute. Only a minute.
Tomas will want the light at half past.

— R.
item.match.desc: A single match with a red head.
item.match.name: Match
item.net.desc: A fishing net, straightened out at last.
item.net.name: Net
item.note.desc: A note to yourself, in your own hand.
item.note.name: R.'s note
item.oar.desc: An ash oar, worn smooth at the grip. One of a pair, you suspect.
item.oar.name: Oar
item.oar2.desc: The pair of the oar you already carry.
item.oar2.name: Second oar
item.oil.desc: A bottle of lamp oil, three-quarters full.
item.oil.name: Lamp oil
item.oilcan.desc: A long-spouted oilcan, half full. Good for anything that has seized.
item.oilcan.name: Oilcan
item.patch.desc: A rag soaked in tar, thick and black. It would seal a hull.
item.patch.name: Tar patch
item.pell_jar.desc: A pickle jar, and Pell in it, with the air of a fish on an expedition. He claims the brine is not his fault.
item.pell_jar.name: Pell's jar
item.pocket_watch.desc: The watch ticks again. When you press it, it carries you between Then and Now.
item.pocket_watch.name: Pocket watch
item.punch.desc: A small steel punch, for tickets.
item.punch.name: Ticket punch
item.rag.desc: A clean, dry rag, folded square.
item.rag.name: Rag
item.small_fish.desc: A small silver fish, still cold from the lake.
item.small_fish.name: Small fish
item.stem.name: Winding stem
item.tar.desc: A lump of tar, softened by the lantern's warmth. It sticks to everything except the thing you want it on.
item.tar.name: Soft tar
item.ticket.desc: A night-ferry ticket for one crossing. The date on it is tomorrow's.
item.ticket.name: Ferry ticket
item.ticket.text:
NIGHT FERRY
One crossing
Valid: tomorrow
item.ticket_ok.desc: Punched for the last crossing. The date on it is today's.

item.ticket_ok.text:
NIGHT FERRY
One crossing
Valid: today
item.timetable.desc: A timetable of the night ferry.
item.timetable.name: Ferry timetable
item.tomas_note.desc: A note from the bottle, stained and soft with water.
item.tomas_note.name: Tomas's note

I'll steer by the bell.

— T.
item.watch.desc: A pocket watch, stopped at 4:19, its glass cracked. The winding stem is missing.
item.watch.name: Pocket watch (stopped)
look.armchair: An armchair by the fire. When you put your hand on the seat, it is still warm.
look.barometer: A barometer. The needle points firmly at STORMY, and has done for a long time.
look.barrel: A barrel of something that has long since gone to rust-coloured water.
look.barrel_d: A barrel, sealed and heavy. It sloshes faintly: only water.
look.bed: A narrow iron bed, neatly made, as if its owner meant to come back to it.
look.bedside: A bedside table, a ring of old tea on its top.
look.bench: A workbench, scarred from years of work.
look.bollard: A cast-iron bollard, furred with old rope.
look.cal_behind: Bare wall, and a pin-hole where something was once fixed.
look.clockwork: Gears and weights, the slow machinery that turns the lens.
look.coal: A coal scuttle. Nothing has been burned here for a long time. Nothing but paper.
look.coil: A coil of rope, stiff with salt. It has been coiled the same way for years.
look.desk: A heavy desk. Ink-stained, scarred with years of elbows.
look.desk_w: A heavy desk, hollowed by years of elbows.
look.end_water: Black water, unmoving. The fog lies on it like cloth.
look.far_light: The far light, a thumbnail of grey on the horizon. Dark.
look.gears_look: The great gears, still and cold.
look.generic.2: It doesn't have anything to say.
look.generic.3: You look. It looks like itself.
look.heron_calm: The heron stands very still, as if it had never left the painting.
look.jetty_lamp: A lamp-post with a cold lamp. Someone used to light it every evening.
look.jetty_water: The water is flat as a table. It has not moved since you can remember.
look.lens_look: A drum of prisms around the lamp.
look.life_ring: A life ring, red and white, the paint cracked. It has never been used.
look.log_left: Earlier pages: weather, oil, small notes in a neat hand.
look.oar_stand: An umbrella stand for oars. Only the one oar left in it.
look.oil_tank: The oil reservoir for the lamp.
look.pegboard: A pegboard of tools, each hung in its own outline. One outline is empty.
look.piling: A salt-grey piling, scored by ropes.
look.pipe: Brass pipes, bound with green, running up through the ceiling toward the lamp.
look.rack: An empty oar rack. Everything that belonged here has been taken, or never was.
look.rocks: Black rocks, slick with rain. The boat is tied just out of sight, behind them.
look.ropes: Coiled rope, two cork buoys, one red, one yellow.
look.stair_steps: Iron-edged stone steps, worn into shallow dishes by years of one person's feet.
look.table: A little round table, kept for the bowl and nothing else.
look.tin_inside: Nails, washers, a bent spoon. The kind of tin where small things go to be lost.
look.tower: The lighthouse rises into the rain, striped red and white where the weather hasn't taken the paint.
look.trunk: A sea-trunk with a rusted lock. It won't open, and doesn't seem to want to.
look.vase: Dry reeds in a vase. They rattle when the air moves, and the air is not moving.
look.wardrobe: A wardrobe, locked, with a keeper's oilskins hanging behind the door.
look.window_lb: A narrow window onto the dark.
look.window_q: The window looks out on rain, and a lake that doesn't move.
look.window_s: A narrow window, running with rain. The lake beyond is flat as slate.
look.window_s2: A narrow window, running with rain.
look.window_sea: The great seaward window: the whole lake from this height, flat and black.
look.window_sl: The storm throws itself at the glass.
look.window_w: The watch-room window: the whole lake, in every direction.
look.window_wb: Rain on the glass, and the dark lake beyond.
mem.1.title: The Quarrel
mem.2.title: Lessons
mem.3.title: The Storm
mem.4.title: Half Past Four
mem.5.title: Still Water
mem1.1: Evening. The lamp is lit and the stove is warm. Tomas has his coat on, and his bag by the door.
mem1.2: "I'm leaving the lake, Ruth. For good. Come with me."
mem1.3: You don't look up. "I can't leave the light."
mem1.4: "The light doesn't need you. I do."
mem1.5: You say something. You can't remember it now, only that it was worse than no.
mem1.6: The door closes. The lamp gutters, and steadies.
mem2.1: You were nine. Tomas was sixteen, patient in a way he never was on land.
mem2.2: "Pull with your back, Ruth, not your arms. Slow."
mem2.3: "The lake is always the same lake. It's the rower who changes."
mem2.4: You rowed in a circle for an hour. He didn't once take the oar from you.
mem2.5: "There. Feel that? That's the water letting you."
mem2.6: That was the best afternoon of your life, and you didn't know it.
mem3.1: 02:00. The storm comes up from the west, fast. Tomas takes the last crossing anyway.
mem3.2: He steers by the light, the way he always has.
mem3.3: He looks up for it. There is no light.
mem3.4: He steers for it anyway, because it has always been there.
mem3.5: 04:30. The deepest water on the lake.
mem4.1: 4:19. You have been awake since yesterday. The chair is warm.
mem4.2: Only a minute, you tell yourself, and close your eyes.
mem4.4: You wake with your cheek on the logbook. Far out on the water, a ferry's lights are going down.
mem4.5: You never forgave yourself. You burned your letters. You left yourself notes, signed with one letter, and kept coming back to the same jetty.
mem5.1: After, you came here every night.
mem5.2: You stood at the end of the jetty, and looked at the water.
mem5.3: The lake never moved. You never said it.
mem5.4: A moth came every night to the lantern, and sat on your hand, and waited.
nb.bell.text: The buoy rings: long, short, short, long. The ripples on the water keep the same rhythm.
nb.bell.title: The bell buoy
nb.clock_fish.text: A tiny fish is engraved on the clock face, beside the four. Pell: "Both hands pointed straight at me."
nb.clock_fish.text2: A tiny fish beside the four. Both hands pointed at it. The clock stopped at 4:20.
nb.clock_fish.title: The stopped clock
nb.floats.text: Four floats on dark water, left to right: red with stripes, green with dots, pale with chevrons, yellow and plain.
nb.floats.title: The floats
nb.mirror.text: Below, the room is a reflection, turned around. What you change there appears Above, reversed.
nb.mirror.title: Above and Below
nb.shapes.text: Four shapes in the water, upside down, left to right: an eye, a moon, a fish, a bell.
nb.shapes.title: Shapes in the lake
nb.tide.text: At 04:20 the water stood at 172 cm.
nb.tide.title: Tide table
nb.valves.text: From the keeper's log: valve settings for the night, 3 · 1 · 4. The last line breaks off: "Tomas due at half past four. Must stay aw"
nb.valves.title: Valve settings
notebook.empty: Nothing in here yet. The notebook sketches what you have seen, never what it means.
notebook.title: Keeper's notebook
notebook.updated: The notebook has a new sketch.
pause.title: Paused
satchel.full: The satchel is full. Something has to be used up first.
settings.hotspot_glow: Highlight what the cursor is over
settings.title: Settings
ticket.pick_both: Pick an hour and a minute first.
title.confirm_new: Starting a new game replaces your current save. Begin again?
use.bottle.key: You can't pick a bottle out of a tree with a key.
use.bottle_cork.key: You can't pick a cork with a key.
use.bowl.key: Pell regards the key with contempt. He's a fish, not a locksmith.
use.bowl.match: Pell recoils from the match. "Fish. Water. Do the arithmetic."
use.bowl.oil: Pell is not a lamp. He says so.
use.candle.key: The key has nothing to do with the candle.
use.chain_lock.key: The padlock wants numbers, not a key.
use.clock.match: The match is for something that burns, not for something that ticks.
use.coat.key: You have already found everything the coat has to give.
use.crank.oar: It's a winch, not a boat.
use.door.key: The key was meant for something with a drawer.
use.drawer.food: Feeding a drawer. Pell would never let you hear the end of it.
use.drawer.match: A match won't open a lock.
use.drawer.oilcan: You oil the rust as best you can, but years of salt don't give way to a single can of oil. In another time, the drawer might not need it.
use.drawer_now.oilcan: You oil the rust as best you can, but years of salt don't give way to a single can of oil. In another time, the drawer might not need it.
use.generic.4: You try it. The room is unimpressed.
use.glass.ash: Ash on glass. It slides off, and leaves a smear.
use.grate.candle_lit: You hold the candle to the grate. The ash is far too cold to catch.
use.grate_b.key: A key, in a grate? No.
use.heron.key: The heron looks at the key, then at you. It already has a very low opinion of you.
use.heron.net: You can't net a heron. Anyone could tell you that.
use.heron_mast.net: You can't net a heron standing on a mast.
use.hole.rag: A dry rag in a hole won't hold the lake out. It needs tar.
use.hook_left.key: The hook has no use for a key.
use.hull_hole.rag: A dry rag in a hole won't hold the lake out. It needs tar.
use.jar.key: The jar doesn't want a key. It wants a reason to stay calm.
use.lantern_desk.candle_lit: It's easier to light a lantern you're holding.
use.lantern_desk.oil: It's easier to fill a lantern you're holding.
use.lockplate.key: The key was meant for something with a drawer.
use.log_torn.stem: The stem has nothing to do with a book.
use.mirror.candle_lit: The mirror shows you a candle. A moment late.
use.painting.match: A match won't last long enough to show you a whole painting.
use.painting_surface.key: You can't unlock a painting. Believe me, you want to.
use.painting_surface.match: A match won't last long enough to show you a whole painting.
use.pell.key: Pell regards the key with contempt. He's a fish, not a locksmith.
use.pell.oil: Pell is not a lamp. He says so.
use.photo.candle_lit: You hold the flame to the photograph. Nothing new comes out of the dark.
use.sill.candle_lit: A candle in a window is just a candle. A lantern in a window is a lighthouse.
use.sill.lantern: A dark lantern in a window is only a lantern. It needs oil and a flame first.
use.tar_pot.oil: Oil and tar. Nobody has ever needed that.
world.log_1: 02:00. Wind south-west and rising. Tomas has taken the last crossing regardless. I told him. He doesn't listen.
world.log_2:
Valves for the night, as the keeper before me wrote:
3 · 1 · 4
world.log_3: 04:00. Lamp low. The oil is slow to come up. I'll sit a minute.
world.log_4: Tomas due at half past four. Must stay aw
world.tide_foot: levels in centimetres, by the clock
